finding: Adding `- 'sdk'` to the path filter (line 23) is necessary but NOT sufficient: the job's `actions/checkout@v4` carries no `submodules:` input, while three sibling workflows (hub-smoke, server-release, desktop-release) explicitly set `submodules: recursive`. On the change class this edit exists to catch — a gitlink-only PR where `src-app/ui/**` is untouched — the `sdk/` directory is checked out EMPTY. `package-lock.json` resolves `@ziee/kit` -> `sdk/packages/kit` and `@ziee/gallery` -> `sdk/packages/gallery` (15 lock references), so `npm ci` cannot complete, and `playwright.visual.config.ts` imports `@ziee/gallery/scripts/lib/run-key.mjs` at module load, so the run cannot even resolve its port. The newly-enabled trigger fires a job that structurally cannot test the kit it was enabled for. Fix: `with: submodules: recursive` on the checkout step.

The logical-direction conversion is NOT complete across the files that compose InputGroupAddon. `CommandInput` applies `*:data-[slot=input-group-addon]:pl-2!` — a PHYSICAL padding-left, with `!important`, keyed off the very logical slot the kit just converted. Measured on the live gallery with the real class strings: (a) LTR, it beats `has-[>button]:ps-1`, so inside any CommandInput the addon is 32.00px wide with the child inset 9.00px from the group's outer edge instead of 28.00px / 5.00px — the new conditional tightening this diff introduces is dead there; (b) RTL, `ps-2` resolves to padding-right while `pl-2!` still paints padding-left, so they STACK: padding-left 8px + padding-right 8px, the search-icon addon measures 32.00px wide in RTL vs 24.00px in LTR, and an 8.00px gap appears between the icon and the input that LTR does not have. The kit file's own comment names `physical padding does not flip under RTL although data-align is expressed in logical terms` as the reason for the fix, then leaves the one in-tree override of that slot physical.

The spec's header claims it measures `BOTH inline-start and inline-end addons ... the two variants are written as a symmetric pair, so a guard on one of them lets the other rot`. Measured: the gallery renders ZERO inline-start addons. At 390px and 1280px, dir=ltr, all 9 `[data-slot=input-group-addon]` carry `data-align="inline-end"` (byAlign {inline-end: 9}); dir=rtl gives 8 and 9, again all inline-end; kbd children = 0. `probeGroups` silently `continue`s on a missing align (line 97), and the two vacuity guards only assert `groups.length > 0` (line 155) and `hasButtonChild > 0` (line 163) — neither can notice that half the matrix was never populated. So the inline-start half of the guard, and the entire `has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5/pe-1.5` half of the change, are vacuous; the falsifiability control (line 44) likewise re-injects only the `inline-end` rule. The spec proves exactly the rot it says it prevents.

The containment defect was fixed and guarded on the INLINE axis only; the identical violation persists on the BLOCK axis, unfixed and unmeasured. Measured on every real input-group at 390px and 1280px, LTR and RTL: group border box 32.00px tall (`h-8`), addon 36.00px tall — the addon bleeds exactly 2.00px above and 2.00px below the group's border box, and each group reports `scrollHeight - clientHeight = 3`. Cause is the same shape as the fixed one: the addon's base `py-1.5` (12px) plus a 24px `icon-xs` button inside an `h-8` box. The new spec measures only `scrollWidth - clientWidth` and only horizontal edges, so its own prose (`the kit InputGroup addon must sit INSIDE its group`) is proven for one axis and asserted for the other.

DESIGN_SYSTEM.md states the logical-direction rule is `Enforced on new/changed code by scripts/lint-logical-direction.mjs`, but that gate cannot see the kit at all. `sdk/packages/config/src/lint/logical-direction.mjs` scans only changed files whose repo-relative path contains one of `PATH_INCLUDE`, defaulting to `src-app/ui/src/` + `src-app/desktop/ui/src/`; ziee's script passes no `--path-include`. It also derives its file set from `git diff` in the PARENT repo, where the whole submodule is a single gitlink, so no file under `sdk/` is ever a candidate. The entire kit — the file this diff fixes and the `pl-2!` / `pr-8` / `ml-auto` / `right-2` it leaves behind — is outside the only mechanical gate for this rule, and the diff adds no `--path-include=sdk/packages/` (or equivalent) to close it. That is why this class of defect had to be found by hand, and nothing stops the next one.

`ComboboxContent` keys PHYSICAL slide-in directions off LOGICAL side values: `data-[side=inline-end]:slide-in-from-left-2 data-[side=inline-start]:slide-in-from-right-2`. Under RTL an `inline-end` popup is positioned physically to the LEFT of its anchor yet animates in from the left — i.e. out from underneath itself — and `inline-start` mirrors the error. This is the exact `physical utility keyed off a logical attribute` pattern the fixed file's comment names as the defect, one file away in the primary consumer of the addon that was fixed, and untouched by the diff. (The `data-[side=left]` / `data-[side=right]` pair beside it is correct — those side values ARE physical.)

`ComboboxItem` reserves the check-indicator gutter with physical `pr-8 pl-1.5` and paints the indicator with `absolute right-2` (line 168). Measured with a real combobox open in the gallery: computed padding-left 6px / padding-right 32px, IDENTICAL in `dir=ltr` and `dir=rtl` (item width 214.00px both). So in RTL the 32px gutter and the check itself sit on the LEADING edge while the trailing edge gets 6px — every option row is mirrored wrong. Same file and same component family the diff certifies as RTL-correct; the new spec measures only the InputGroup box, never the popup it opens.

The new copy is inaccurate for one of the four cases it enumerates, and throws away information the backend already computed. `PromptFileError::Empty` is documented in validate.rs as `Reads successfully but is EMPTY` and is a distinct arm from `Unreadable`, so `This step's prompt file can't be read - it may be ... be empty` contradicts the backend's own model: an empty file reads fine. The list also omits the commonest remaining `Unreadable` cause, a permissions failure (`read_to_string` -> EACCES), which the generic lead clause covers only by accident. Worse, `CopyContext.message` already carries the exact reason and the exact path (`prompt_file 'x.md' is empty` / `prompt_file 'x.md' cannot be read from the bundle: <os error>`), and other entries in this file do consume ctx — but the new CopyFn is written `() =>`, discarding both. The author is handed a four-way guess about a file the server named unambiguously.

The remedy is not actionable on this surface and breaks the voice its immediate neighbours establish. Every other entry for a finding whose control the builder does not render ends with WHERE to act: `WORKFLOW_BAD_STEP_ID` and `WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE_STEP_ID` end `...in the workflow file and import it again`; `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH` ends `...drop the file from the workflow and import it again`; `_UNSAFE`/`_ESCAPE` end `name a file that is stored with this workflow instead`. The new string ends `Check the path and the file, or type the prompt in directly` - `check` is a diagnostic instruction, not an act, and stepForms.ts states plainly that `the builder renders no prompt-file control`, so neither the path nor the file is reachable from this page. The file's own header rule is `say what the PERSON must do, not what the schema requires`. The rationale comment faults the old copy for being `a remedy the author could not act on for three of those four cases` and then ships a remedy the author cannot act on for all four.

`or type the prompt in directly` walks the author into a different blocking finding, and contradicts copy rendered on the same screen. `promptSuppliedByFile` returns true for ANY non-empty `prompt_file`, including a broken one, so while this panel line is showing, AgentStepForm/LlmStepForm/LlmMapStepForm are simultaneously rendering `PROMPT_FROM_FILE_NOTE` as the prompt field's description: `This step takes its wording from a prompt file in the workflow bundle, so there is nothing to type here.` Two contradictory instructions about the same box. And if the author follows the panel, `prompt_source` then sees both an inline prompt and a `prompt_file` and reports `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH`. `PROMPT_FROM_FILE_NOTE` warns about exactly this trap (`Type something to override it - but then remove the file, since a step cannot use both`); the new copy, which is the one telling them to type, does not.

Violates the file's stated length rule. The HUMAN_COPY header says `stay one sentence where possible - the panel is dense`; the new string is two sentences and 168 characters, the longest entry in the map, and the only one phrased as a four-way `it may be ...` maybe-list rather than a statement of what is wrong. In a dense validation panel that lists one line per finding, this is the entry most likely to wrap to three lines at 390px.

The comment's stated rationale does not hold for the branch it introduces. It faults the old values for being `off the 4px spacing scale` and calls the replacements `Grid-aligned logical padding`, but `ps-1.5`/`pe-1.5` is 6px - a 2px half-step, not on the 4px grid DESIGN_SYSTEM.md defines (`every gap-N/p-N/m-N is N x 4px`; `Stay on the scale`). Measured 6.00px in LTR and RTL for the kbd shape. The change is still an improvement, but one third of the new triple (8 / 4 / 6) is off-grid, so grid-alignment cannot be the reason it is right.

The variants document a rule the CSS does not implement for the combined child shape. `has-[>button]:ps-1` and `has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5` have equal specificity (0,2,0), so when an addon holds BOTH a button and a kbd, source order decides and the KBD value wins. Measured for the button+kbd shape: padding-left 6px (not 4px) and the button child sits 7.00px from the group's outer edge instead of 5.00px, in LTR; mirrored identically in RTL. The comment above states `4px beside a button, 6px beside a kbd`, which is not what an addon containing a button actually gets in that configuration. Cosmetically minor, but the addon+shortcut composition (`[&>kbd]` styling exists precisely for it) is the one the kit advertises and no test covers it.

The commit is titled `finish the logical-direction conversion on InputGroup`, but the block half of the same rule set is both still physical and INVERTED relative to the inline half it converts. `has-[>[data-align=block-end]]:[&>input]:pt-3` and `has-[>[data-align=block-start]]:[&>input]:pb-3` put the input's padding on the side AWAY from the addon; the inline pair (`ps-1.5`/`pe-1.5`) puts it on the side FACING the addon, which is what produces the 6px addon-to-text gap the comment cites. Measured with a synthetic block-start addon: input padding-top 0px / padding-bottom 12px, addon-to-input gap 0.00px, 12.00px of dead space at the far end; block-end mirrors it. So a block addon abuts the input's text with no gap while the far edge carries 12px of nothing.

The addon's `icon-xs` control measures exactly 24.00 x 24.00 CSS px in every real input-group at 390px, in both LTR and RTL - precisely at the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA) Target Size (Minimum) floor, with zero slack. The diff does not change that size, but it does reduce the addon's own inline padding beside a button from 8px to 4px and moves the button 0.80px further inside the group, so the enclosing box now has less room than before for any future growth of the control. Separately, because the addon is 36.00px tall inside a 32.00px group, 2.00px of the button's 24px box sits outside the control's painted border on the top and bottom - the target extends past the affordance it belongs to.

`InputGroupAddon` renders `role="group"` with no accessible name, nested directly inside `InputGroup`'s own unnamed `role="group"`. Two nested unnamed groups per text control is pure AT noise: neither conveys anything, and the inner one wraps a single icon or button. Unchanged by the diff, but it is the element the diff re-specifies, and the addon's `onClick` focus-the-input behaviour (line 79) is likewise keyboard-unreachable and unannounced. A plain `div` (or an `aria-hidden` presentational wrapper for the icon-only case) would say the same thing more quietly.

REJECTED: candidate that the gate allow-list edit is a no-op because `src-app/ui/scripts/gate-ui.mjs` hardcodes its spec list (layout/states/overlays + gallery under VISUAL_SNAPSHOTS) and never reads `visualSpecs`. Read the wiring rather than assuming: `package.json:192` maps `gate:ui` to `../../sdk/packages/gallery/scripts/gate-ui.mjs`, which spreads `...CFG.visualSpecs` (line 185) from `resolveGalleryConfig(cwd)` -> `src-app/ui/gallery.config.json`. The in-app script is a stale duplicate that nothing invokes. `npm run gate:ui` WILL run `input-group-overflow.spec.ts`; the config edit is correct and sufficient for the gate.

REJECTED: candidate that the inline conversion is asymmetric, leaves an overhang, or changes size unintentionally. Measured all 6 child shapes (button / kbd / icon / text / empty / button+kbd) x both aligns x LTR and RTL, at 390px and 1280px: the addon's inset from the group's outer edge is exactly 1.00px (the border) in all 24 cells, `scrollWidth - clientWidth = 0` in all 24 cells, and each shape's resolved padding mirrors exactly between directions (button 4px, kbd 6px, icon/text/empty 8px; addon widths 28.00 / 26.03 / 24.00 / 22.00 / 8.00 / 58.03px identical either way). The overhang is genuinely gone and the pair is genuinely symmetric.

REJECTED: candidate that the change alters tap-target size, focus ring, or hit area. Focus styling lives entirely on the group (`has-[[data-slot=input-group-control]:focus-visible]:ring-3 ...:ring-ring/50`) and is untouched; the button measures 24.00 x 24.00px with a 7px radius before and after; only the addon's own click-to-focus-the-input strip moves, from [group.right-28.2, group.right+3.8] to [group.right-29, group.right-1] - i.e. it stops overhanging the painted control and now sits wholly inside it, which is strictly better. No tap target shrank.

REJECTED: candidate that the surviving `pt-3`/`pb-3` on the `block-*` branches is an RTL bug of the same kind as the fixed `pl`/`pr`. Block-axis physical properties do not flip with `dir`, only with `writing-mode`, and Tailwind ships no `padding-block-start`/`padding-block-end` utilities, so `pt`/`pb` are the only available spelling. The RTL half of this concern is inert; what IS wrong there is the sign inversion, filed separately.

REJECTED: candidate that `- 'sdk'` is the wrong path-filter spelling for a submodule (that it needs `sdk/**` or `sdk/*`). A gitlink change is reported by GitHub's PR files API at the literal path `sdk` with no trailing segment - `sdk/**` would in fact NOT match it, while the bare `sdk` pattern does. The filter line itself is correct; the defect is the missing `submodules: recursive` on the checkout.

REJECTED: candidate that the new copy leaks developer jargon. Measured against the file's own three rules, it passes the vocabulary one cleanly: it names no YAML key, no Rust field and no wire type; `a folder rather than a file` and `not be text` are plain-English renderings of EISDIR and an invalid-UTF-8 read; `prompt file` is the same term the neighbouring PROMPT_BOTH and PROMPT_FROM_FILE_NOTE entries already use. The problems with this string are accuracy, actionability and length, not jargon.

REJECTED: candidate that the addon's width change causes a layout shift or new clipping at the 390px viewport the residual named. Measured: addon width 28.00px and group horizontal overflow 0 at BOTH 390px and 1280px in both directions; the group is `flex` with a `flex-1` input, so the net +0.80px of inline size is absorbed by the input, not by the group. The spec's choice to probe both widths is right for a different reason (proving width-independence), not because 390px behaves differently.
